subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I need to put together a single TypeScript module using the SDK, relying only on the documented helper APIs like builder construction, joints, chains, sweeps, lofts, and related geometry functions, while keeping things concise and correct given the limited reference available.

I'm genuinely unsure of exact signatures for many of these functions—things like how parent joints are referenced or how sweep options are structured—so I'll make the most plausible guesses, favoring passing joint handles directly and standard option objects, while keeping the usage minimal to reduce risk of errors.

Given the uncertainty, I'll lean toward combining THREE.js geometries with b.stick, since documentation confirms it takes a geometry, color, and a hit/frame argument, which lets me seat parts along a facing axis using frame(at, dir, up) rather than guessing at undocumented part-building calls.

Now I'm sketching the overall knight structure: a hip root around 1 meter up, a spine chain rising to the head, neck and shoulder joints, with arms and legs built through limb helpers connecting lengths and bends, keeping total joint count manageable. For the actual geometry, I'm placing cylinders and capsule-like shapes along each limb segment, accepting some guesswork on the exact capsule signature while favoring a consistent pattern of defining points, radius, and color for each piece.

For the head I'm shaping a great helm using a tapered cylinder oriented along the facing direction, then moving on to plan the overall module at roughly 250 compact lines covering materials like steel, gold, crimson, blue, silver, and wood, staying within a reasonable material limit. I'm also working out how to render a griffin emblem on the surcoat, opting to build a 2D outline of the griffin silhouette and extrude it onto the surface rather than risk an uncertain decal/texture API.

Now I'm figuring out the torn cape by stretching a membrane between a polyline at the shoulder and a jagged bottom edge, sketching the sword from a simple rod with a boxy grip and blade, and shaping the kite shield as an extruded outline with a raised griffin emblem on its face. For the plume I'm adding one or more spikes jutting from the helm, and for extra detail I'm planning small darker boxes as battle scratches and thin gold strips along the shoulder pauldrons as filigree instead of a more complex looped stud pattern.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: hips, chest, neck, and head joints stacked vertically, then branching shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints for each arm (shield arm on one side, sword arm on the other) and hip, knee, ankle joints for each leg, all positioned with specific coordinates so the knight faces forward with the sword hand held out front. I'm also sketching a small helper function to place geometry at a given position and direction so I can attach body parts consistently along these joint frames.

Writing capsule/geometry helpers...

I'm planning the visual details: dented and scratched steel plating scattered across the breastplate using randomized thin boxes, a color palette (steel, gold, crimson, leather, black visor slit, etc.), and a cape built from a membrane stretched between back-shoulder points down to a bottom edge polyline.

I'm working out matching point counts for the cape's top and bottom edges, a griffin emblem extruded onto the chest surcoat with positioned outline points, and a kite-shaped shield outline held at the character's left side.

For the sword, I'm positioning the hilt at the right wrist and extending a blade shape forward and upward, considering whether to use a capsule or box geometry for the blade since the exact helper signature is uncertain. Then I'm figuring out the plume's base position and direction vector for a spike shape on the helmet.

Now I'm sketching out the full armor build: the great helm as a forward-facing cylinder with an eye slit, the breastplate and surcoat with the griffin emblem, pauldrons as stacked discs with gold filigree, tassets and leg plates, and scattered dents and scratches for weathering detail. I'm also planning the joint hierarchy from hips through chest, neck, head, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles before writing the final code.
